title: Matched recurrent organization under varied-cadence posterior transfer
research_question: Does four-block recurrence reduce d=4 joint-posterior KL versus a degree/self-loop/resource-matched random-mask GRU under the same varied-cadence training?
strongest_rejection_reason: A structural d=4 difference may reflect optimization, graph mixing or nuisance-duration distribution shift rather than semantic hypothesis trajectories.
hypothesis: M3 reduces C0 d=4 final joint-posterior KL by more than 0.05 nat after adequate d=1 learning and control headroom, without material IID KL or H-accuracy cost.
intervention: Four independent recurrent blocks versus non-diagonally degree- and self-loop-preserving rewired recurrence.
controls: same hidden state and active/allocated parameters for M3/C0
dataset: Hidden-source exact-posterior task; train d=0/1/2, final IID d=1, primary OOD d=4, secondary d=8; fresh streams
metrics: final joint KL to exact posterior
resource_matching: M3/C0 exact active/allocated parameter, state, input schedule and dense-operation match; M1 same state/allocated/dense execution but more effective parameters.
interpretation: d4 C0-minus-M3 final joint KL mean -0.001356 nat, paired-seed 95% CI [-0.002990,+0.000120]. C0 mean KL 0.012463 failed the registered >=0.07 headroom guard; matching and IID adequacy passed.
limitations: one synthetic generator and one fixed test stream
analytical compute proxy is not measured full training FLOPs
next_action: STOP_MECHANISM_ESCALATION; require actual primary-control calibration before another useful-effect threshold, and audit PF-RNN/RIMs before candidate-trajectory claims.
